The Supreme Court’s decision in Roe v. Wade is highly controversial because it held the Texas abortion law unconstitutional as violating a woman’s right to privacy. The majority reasoned that the Fourteenth Amendment’s protection of personal liberty includes a right to privacy broad enough to cover a woman’s decision whether to end her pregnancy, so Texas’s restriction intruded on that right. That privacy holding, not a failure to consider medical evidence, is the ground of the decision.
